propertyFacts.label: Empirical lift-off resist-thickness threshold
propertyFacts.scope: For the approximately 10 nm QDs used in this study; not a universal final thickness.

source_locator.locator: MAIN PDF p.3 / printed 7483, Optimized lift-off and nanoscale patterning

propertyFacts.label: Authors’ proposed sidewall effect
propertyFacts.value: The LB film bends and breaks around resist edges; deposition onto exposed sidewalls lowers QD density remaining on the substrate after lift-off.

source_locator.locator: MAIN PDF p.2 / printed 7482, Experimental processing scheme and QD material

propertyFacts.qualifier: Source mechanism and schematic; no atomic structure measured.

propertyFacts.label: Resist-thickness range for the source pure-acetone limitation
propertyFacts.scope: SI states that pure acetone cannot lift off an LB QD film on resist below approximately 1 μm. The cited earlier optical-lithography result is separate historical context.

source_locator.locator: SI PDF p.3 / printed S3, S2 lift-off solvent rationale

propertyFacts.qualifier: Source qualitative limitation for LB films; no complete separate pure-acetone control recipe or count supplied.

propertyFacts.label: Authors’ rationale for the mixed solvent
propertyFacts.value: Acetone dissolves the resist; toluene stabilizes lifted organic-ligand-passivated QDs and helps prevent redeposition. Mixture ratio balances resist dissolution with QD stabilization.

source_locator.locator: SI PDF p.3 / printed S3, S2 lift-off solvent rationale

propertyFacts.label: Source thickness rule of thumb
propertyFacts.value: A resist thickness about twice the QD diameter including passivating oleic-acid ligands can be lifted off effectively with the optimized 1:4 mixture.

source_locator.locator: SI PDF p.6 / printed S6, S3 rule of thumb

propertyFacts.qualifier: A qualitative source design rule; no ligand thickness, precise coated-QD diameter or independently computed threshold is assigned.

general_background.title: Thermodynamics and kinetics
general_background.summary: Thermodynamics describes which states are energetically favoured, while kinetics governs how quickly a system can move between them. A change can be favourable yet proceed slowly when an activation barrier or limited transport restricts the pathway.
